method: Pages fetched with plain curl (default headers, about one a second) from experienceleague.adobe.com and developer.adobe.com; the HTML held the article text directly, so no .md or JSON fallback was needed. Follow-up pages were found from links on those pages and from the Experience League and developer.adobe.com site lists a sibling check had already saved. Every quote was proven present in its saved file with the same matcher as handoff/2026-11-17/evidence_page/tools/verify.py (a quote with '...' is matched as parts in order). business.adobe.com and partners.adobe.com were not attempted. helpx.adobe.com's ColdFusion guide answered with a forward to guides.adobe.com, which is not an accepted site, and was not followed.

records.assistant: ChatGPT, as a place to run paid ads (through OpenAI's ad system). Not Claude. This is an ad channel, not an assistant a person chats with to reach Adobe.
records.what_adobe_says: A client's marketing team can build ChatGPT ads (the 'Chat Card' format) inside GenStudio for Performance Marketing: generate on-brand copy, run brand and channel checks, get approvals, then send the approved ad to an ad group that already exists in the client's OpenAI ad account. The last checks and the launch happen in OpenAI's own Ads Manager. GenStudio does not create the campaign or ad group. First the client needs its own OpenAI ad account and a key from it, and a GenStudio system manager pastes that key into GenStudio's settings. In the tool this fits the existing 'Ad platforms' outside system (GenStudio already sends ads to Meta, Google and others the same way); it is not a ChatGPT or Claude 'connector'.
